Subject: Observability ride-along: telemetry onboarding & operational runbook

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the kickoff this morning. As discussed, attached is a compact handoff packet that outlines the telemetry and operational milestones we should run through during the next two weeks. High-level goals:

- Validate dashboard coverage for customer-facing SLAs and internal SLOs
- Walk tracing hooks for the top three request paths (CreateClaim, DocumentUpload, SummarizeReport)
- Confirm alert routing & escalation flow for P1/P2 errors and noisy noise suppression rules
- Run a dry-run of the on-call handoff and the primary runbook for common failure modes

Proposed ride-along schedule (30–60m sessions):
1) May 19 — Dashboard tour & metric mapping (owner: Marissa)
2) May 20 — Tracing hooks validation with dev pair (owner: Aditya)
3) May 21 — Alert playbook and runbook dry-run (owner: Neha/Tessa)

I've included a mockup dashboard and a runbook template you can preview. Can you confirm the attendees on your side and whether we should add a security SME for the runbook dry-run?

Attachments: telemetry-handoff-packet.pdf, dashboard-mockup.png

Best,
Neha Kapoor

Team —

Thanks for the heads-up. I'll run the dashboard tour and will be explicit about which charts are customer-facing vs. ops-only. Draft checklist for the dashboard session:

- Verify metric names & tags (service, env, region)
- Confirm top-level SLAs: 99.9% success rate for CreateClaim (30d window), median latency targets for DocumentUpload
- Synthetic monitors: locations, frequency, and alert thresholds
- Dashboards: link to request traces and error-rate heatmaps
- Evidence: exportable CSVs for compliance (covered under the runbook sec section)

I've attached a quick screenshot of the dashboard mockup and a short pointer to the query that populates the request-latency panel.

Also: Aditya, can you prepare a short checklist for tracing hook verification? Ideally a one-pager that our customers can keep as instrumentation acceptance criteria.

-Marissa

Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference.com>

Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 07:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability ride-along: telemetry onboarding & operational runbook

Quick note from the instrumentation side:

I prepared a 1-page trace acceptance checklist and a minimal snippet customers can add to their SDK integration. Key items:
- Ensure spans propagate request_id and user_id tags
- Sampled traces for 1% production traffic; high-sample for errors
- Annotate external service calls and heavy I/O (file parsing)

Also calling out alert routing assumptions we should validate:
- P1 (system down / API 5xx spike) -> Pager duty route A (primary on-call) + Slack #prod-ops
- P2 (error-rate increase) -> Email + ticket create in Jira (SUP-3241)
- Noise suppression: use adaptive aggregation windows and exclude known benign error codes

I linked the Jira ticket in the packet for on-call runbook items. Happy to demo the snippet during the May 20 morning session.

- Aditya
Senior Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference

----
Attachment: runbook-template.md
